Door-enhancement

Não consigo abrir a porta, é como se ela estivesse sendo puxada e simplesmente volta a fechar toda vez que eu tento abrí-la

corrigir a posição ao segurar a porta (a mão está ficando dentro da porta no meio entre uma maçaneta e outra

seria melhor se ao segurar a maçaneta, ele sempre segurasse da mesma forma e na mesma posição, e se possível encontrar alguma forma de mascarar posicionamentos errados

fixar mão do Miles na maçaneta da porta (impedir que a mão seja movida/girada)

Mesmo esticando a mão direita para segurar a porta eu acabo segurando a câmera

deixar porta menos pesada (mais fácil de mover)

ajustar o quanto precisa afastar a mão que está segurando a maçaneta para que ela se solte da porta (atualmente um movimento pequeno já faz com que a mão pare de segurar a porta, movimento esse que muitas vezes se trata de uma tentativa de mover a porta)

corrigir colisão das mãos (em que os dedos atravessam as portas quando se tenta empurrar)

tirar o quadrado verde guia e o texto guia para abrir portas

aumentar a área em que é possível segurar a porta e adicionar vibração respectivo ao controle quando segurar a porta

porta termina de abrir automaticamente ao puxá-la até certo ponto e soltá-la

ao segurar uma porta aberta e fazer movimento para frente e soltar a porta é fechada automaticamente 

falta amplitude para abrir mais a porta (eu só consigo abrir suficientemente andando, ajustar para que um movimento maior do braço se traduza em uma rotação da porta equivalente (eu consigo abrir muito pouco somente com a mão) não é peso é amplitude

criar escala de rotação, tipo aceleração angular da porta proporcional à velocidade da mão

ao tentar abrir a porta, ela bate no Miles e não abre mais, seria interessante se a porta passasse através do Miles somente para abrí-la (se ela já estiver aberta não é interessante que ela passe através do Miles)

colocar som na porta ao abri-la fisicamente

Let me read the full Doors function lines 716-1200.

Now I understand the existing door system. The user has a long list of issues after the previous commit. Let me parse each request carefully:

1. "Não consigo abrir a porta, é como se ela estivesse sendo puxada e simplesmente volta a fechar toda vez que eu tento abrí-la" - Can't open door, it's as if being pulled and just closes again every time.
2. Fix position when holding door (hand ending up inside door between one knob and another).
3. Better if when holding knob, always holds same way and same position, and if possible mask wrong placements.
4. Fix Miles's hand on the doorknob (prevent hand from being moved/rotated).
5. Even stretching right hand to hold door I end up holding the camera.
6. Make door less heavy (easier to move).
7. Adjust how far to pull hand away while holding knob for it to release (currently small movement releases hand, often an attempt to move door).
8. Fix hand collision (fingers pass through doors when trying to push).
9. Remove green guide square and guide text for opening doors.
10. Increase area where possible to hold door + add controller vibration when holding door.
11. Door automatically finishes opening when pulled to a point and released.
12. When holding an open door and moving forward and releasing, door closes automatically.
13. Lack of amplitude to open door more (can only open enough by walking, adjust so larger arm movement translates to equivalent door rotation — can open very little with hand only) not weight, amplitude.
14. Create rotation scale, angular acceleration proportional to hand speed.
15. When trying to open door, it hits Miles and won't open more; interesting if door passes through Miles only to open (if already open not interesting).
16. Add sound to door when physically opening.

The previous commit attempted many of these but apparently not good enough. We need to improve substantially.

Let me look at the broader architecture: how hands are anchored/rendered, collision, etc. Let's search for s_anchorW and hand rendering. Also look at OLSound_PostByName implementation, and door sound event names available in ol_sound.cpp.
Now let me look at how arm solve uses anchor, and how hands are drawn (hand model). Search for HandAnchorWorld usage.
Now ol_ue3.cpp around 4250-4350 to see anchor solve.
Let me continue to see hand orientation and whether anchor pins orientation.

The arm position is anchored, but wrist orientation is controller-derived. So "fix hand on knob (prevent moved/rotated)" means when anchored to a door handle, we should also pin the wrist/hand orientation to the knob, i.e. expose a special anchor orientation. Currently just position. We can add OLInteract_HandAnchorRotation to blend orientation. But that's more involved. Alternatively set wristTarget to a fixed rotation when holding knob. Let's expose an anchor orientation + weight. This can address "sempre segurasse da mesma forma e na mesma posição" and "fixar mão na maçaneta (impedir movida/girada)".

But the priority: the user's main complaint "can't open door, it just closes again". Let's reason about the physics/control bugs.

Currently grabbing is triggered by s_gripEdge (fresh grip). The hand position is pinned to s_grabFixPt = handW at grab. Effective hand = fixed point + excess beyond 10uu deadzone. Door angle A vs hand angle Aw via spring. Then angular acceleration from hand speed.

Issue 1: door closes again. Why? Possibly because the anchor position pull? Or because auto-finish misfires: if nd->ratio > 0.55 releasing triggers auto-finish; but before release... Hmm. Or because the grab is lost quickly (slipping due to outOfReach/turnedAway) and auto-finish incorrectly closes. Actually the complaint "it's as if being pulled and just closes again every time I try to open it". Could be the door passes through him and then hits...? Or the auto-close logic: when grabbing a door that's already open? Hmm.

Let's think about the physics spring. sign = rev ? 1 : -1. A = ratio*maxA. Hand angle Aw = A + sign*Wrap180(aHand - phi0). Wait phi0 is the panel angle at rest (knob-hinge). When at rest ratio=0, knob at phi0. If rev false, sign=-1, A=0. Door opens by A increasing; panel angle = phi0 + sign*(An-A)? Looking at line 1133: phi0 + sign*(An-A). If sign=-1, opening rotates panel by -A (clockwise). Then the knob's angle becomes phi0 - A. Hand at knob: aHand ≈ phi0 - A. Aw = A + (-1)*Wrap180(aHand - phi0) = A - (aHand - phi0). If aHand=phi0-A, Aw=A - (-A)=2A. That's wrong! Wait let's re-check. At rest A=0, hand at phi0: Aw=0. As door opens with An, hand follows knob at phi0 + sign*An = phi0 - An (sign=-1). Then Aw = An + sign*Wrap180(aHand-phi0) = An + (-1)*( -An) = 2An. So the spring target is 2A, causing the door to keep accelerating/opening? Hmm maybe sign convention different.

Let's derive intent: aHand measured in world. Panel angle after ratio r: phi = phi0 + sign*A (A=r*maxA). The difference from rest panel angle is sign*A. So aHand - phi0 ≈ sign*A. Then Aw should equal A. Given Aw = A + sign*Wrap180(aHand - phi0) = A + sign*(sign*A) = A + A = 2A. That seems a bug — unless phi0 is not rest panel angle but knob angle at max? Let's check what knob and hinge represent. OLUE3_DoorKnobWorld likely returns current knob position? And ratio current. At ratio > 0, knob rotated. Then phi0 = atan2(knob - hinge) is current panel angle, and A = ratio*maxA. The relationship: current panel angle = phi0_rest + sign*A. But phi0 computed from current knob = current panel angle = phi0_rest + sign*A. So aHand - phi0 = hand angle relative to current panel. Aw = A + sign*(aHand - phi0) = A + sign*(relative). If hand at rest panel, relative=0 -> Aw=A correct. If door moves so hand follows, then phi0 updates too, so relative stays. Ah, phi0 is current, not rest. But then A is current ratio too. Hmm: Aw = A + sign*relative; that's angle in ratio-degree space relative to current panel. Good, that's consistent: target angle change from current A based on hand offset from current panel. That makes sense. My earlier derivation conflated. Good.

So the spring drives A toward A + sign*relative. Fine. But there's a subtle issue: phi0 and A are both current; if the hand stays still in world while the door moves toward it, relative changes ⇒ Aw changes by sign... since sign*relative. As door opens (A increases, panel angle changes by sign*A), hand fixed ⇒ relative = aHand - phi_current changes by -sign*dA ⇒ Aw = A + sign*(aHand - phi0) changes by dA - sign*sign*dA = 0. So a stationary hand keeps target the same => door coasts and doesn't follow? Hmm, that means spring target remains constant A0, while current A moves past, so spring pulls back. Wait let's carefully define: phi0(now) = phi_rest + sign*A (current panel). relative = aHand - phi0(now). Aw = A + sign*relative = A + sign*aHand - sign*phi_rest - sign*sign*A = sign*(aHand - phi_rest). Since sign^2=1, A cancels! So Aw = sign*(aHand - phi_rest) — purely hand angle, independent of door. Great. So φ_rest is embedded; but they use phi0 current plus A to reconstruct. Fine. So spring target is hand angle in ratio space. Good.

So when hand moves in a circle around hinge, Aw follows. With fixed grab point, eff = fixed point + excess past deadzone, so movement is measured from grab position.

Now why door closes again? Auto-finish: if released above 0.55, it sets om=+kOpenSwing. kOpenSwing=90. But sign convention: Om positive = ratio increasing (opening), independent. So om +90 => opening. If pushTowardClose, om=-90 → closing. But how is pushTowardClose computed? s_handSpd is recomputed each frame from hand motion; on the release frame, the hand might be moving due to tracking jitter or the player's natural hand movement. Specifically hDir formula uses world tangent tx,ty of current panel and openingDir = rev?1:-1. It computes (prev - current) dot tangent * openingDir > 0. But this is suspect and may be inverted, causing an open door to close automatically on release, which matches "when I try to open it, it's like it's pulled and just closes again". Also item 12: "ao segurar uma porta aberta e fazer movimento para frente e soltar a porta é fechada automaticamente" — this was requested behavior? The list reads like requests/desired fixes. Item 11: auto open when pulled past point and released. Item 12: when holding open door and moving forward and releasing, door closes automatically. So auto-close is desired. But item 1 says door can't open and closes again. The bug could be that auto-finish is erroneously closing.

Wait the list is likely feedback on the already-implemented commit: it enumerates remaining problems AND requests. Some items may be duplicates of previous requests not yet satisfying. Hmm. Actually the user text begins "Door-enhancement" then lists complaints and requests. It is likely a new task set to implement all. Some already partially implemented but buggy. Our job: implement all correctly.

Key issue: "Não consigo abrir a porta, é como se ela estivesse sendo puxada e simplesmente volta a fechar toda vez que eu tento abrí-la" — likely the auto-close triggering or the door stop logic with Miles. Let's examine the door-stop: closing = (Om < 0) || (An < A). When opening Om>0, An>A so not closing. Fine. But when door angle A currently set, and ratio is current open; door may pass through. Fine.

Another likely bug: "the door hits Miles and doesn't open" solved by letting pass while opening. But their closing logic `An < A` could catch when Om positive but An slightly less than A due to spring? An=A+Om*dt; Om>0 => An>A. Fine.

Maybe the actual door cannot open because the game's OLDoor clamps ratio based on collision with Miles? OLUE3_DoorSetRatioAndTarget may fail when Miles in the way, and OLDoor's own tick may pull ratio back? Hmm.

We need to look at the game-side door functions in ol_ue3.cpp to understand ratio semantics and collision.

Knob returns current world position (includes opening), as comment says. Good.

Now the interaction between door and Miles: the game's own OLDoor tick may collide door with Miles? The set-ratio native drops/re-registers navmesh obstacle; the door mesh might physically sweep against Miles and push? The mod adds a stop against hero. The user says door hits Miles and won't open. We made it pass through Miles while opening, but maybe the check uses current ratio A and Om, and the door stops because the game's native or navmesh prevents? Hmm.

Let's consider the more fundamental physics: The door may be colliding with Miles because `An` from the spring is being clamped. The hero stop only when closing. But maybe the sign of opening is inverted for some doors: `closing = (Om < 0) || (An < A)`; if the door opens in negative Om (depending on sign), then opening happens with Om negative and the stop triggers. Wait `An` is the ratio-angle A, not panel angle. Om is dA/dt; opening is An increasing because ratio goes 0->1. Always opening means ratio increasing. So Om>0. Thus closing condition fine. Unless user pushes door further open via pushing (anyPush) which also increases An.

But the game's OLDoor tick could clamp ratio when Miles stands in the door's way? Since we set OpenRatio and Target simultaneously, its tick has nothing to chase, but navmesh obstacle move may fail/push. Not sure.

Let's check git history to see prior attempt/test docs maybe docs mention door tests. Search docs for door.

# Building Outlast VR

## Prerequisites

- Windows 10/11, x64.
- Visual Studio 2022 (Community, Professional, Enterprise, or the standalone Build Tools)
  with the **"Desktop development with C++"** workload installed. `build.bat` locates it
  automatically via `vswhere.exe`.
- No other tools or package managers required. MinHook and Dear ImGui are vendored in
  `third_party/` - nothing to fetch or install separately.

## Build

```
scripts\build.bat
```

Output: `builds\d3d9.dll` (and `builds\d3d9.map`).

The build is a single `cl.exe` invocation (no solution/project file, no CMake) that compiles
the mod's own sources together with the vendored MinHook and Dear ImGui sources, statically
linked (`/MT`), so the resulting DLL needs no separate vcruntime redistributable in the game
folder.

## Deploying

Copy these files into `<Outlast install>\Binaries\Win64\`, next to `OLGame.exe`:

- `builds\d3d9.dll` (just built)
- `openxr_loader.dll` - an x64 build of the official [Khronos OpenXR loader](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenXR-SDK), not built by this repo
- `outlastvr.ini` (see `runtime/outlastvr.ini` for a starting point)

See `release/README.txt` for the installer script and end-user install steps.

## Third-party components

| Component | Location | License |
|---|---|---|
| MinHook | `third_party/minhook` | BSD 2-Clause (see its `LICENSE.txt`) |
| Dear ImGui | `third_party/imgui` | MIT (see its `LICENSE.txt`) |
| OpenXR loader | not vendored, obtained separately | Apache 2.0 |

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Implement the user's full "Door-enhancement" feedback list for the Outlast VR door interaction so doors open reliably, feel lighter, use intuitive hand motion, pin Miles's hand to the handle, support auto-open/close, sound, haptics, and remove door guide visuals/prompts.

## Requirements
- Fix doors that seem to be pulled and close again every time the user tries to open them.
- Fix hand position while holding a door (hand ended up inside the door between knobs).
- Holding the handle should always look consistent and mask bad placements.
- Pin Miles's hand to the doorknob; prevent the hand from being moved/rotated.
- Right hand reaching for a door must not grab the camcorder instead.
- Make doors less heavy/easier to move.
- Increase the hand-away distance required to release the handle; small movements must not release it.
- Fix hand collision (fingers pass through doors when pushing).
- Remove green guide square and guide text for opening doors.
- Increase the grabbable area and add controller vibration while holding the door.
- Door auto-finishes opening when pulled past a point and released.
- Holding an open door, moving forward, and releasing auto-closes it.
- Increase opening amplitude: larger arm motion must translate into equivalent door rotation; it is amplitude, not weight.
- Add rotation scaling / angular acceleration proportional to hand speed.
- Door may pass through Miles while opening, but not when already open/closing.
- Add door sound when physically opening.

## Decisions
- Replace angular hand-position control around the hinge with linear hand travel along the knob's opening tangent, scaled by `kHandleGain = 2.6` deg/uu; this gives amplitude and repeatable rotation.
- Lock wrist orientation while grabbing, rotating it with the door swing via a new anchor-lock/yaw API.
- Release only on grip open, door gone/busy, body turn >45°, knob reach >110 uu, or hand travel >85 uu—not tiny movements.
- Auto-open only when ratio >0.55 and hand was not pulled toward closing; auto-close only when ratio >0.20 and hand moved ≥18 uu toward closing.
- Use real Wwise events found in the installed game: `EV_Opening_Wood_Door`, `EV_Closing_Wood_Door`, `EV_Push_Wood_Door` (bank `WwiseDefaultBank_General_Sound`), replacing nonexistent `DOOR_OPEN`/`DOOR_CLOSE`.
- Allow right-hand door interaction; stow camcorder when the right hand grabs a door; block camcorder grip while near a knob.
- Remove door green ring/teach label and blank out `G_DOORS` UI prompts.

## Work State
### Completed
- Investigated existing door physics, hand IK anchoring, holster/camcorder interaction, Wwise sound banks, and prompt rewriting.
- Located actual Outlast install at `S:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Outlast`.
- Started source edits in `src/ol_interact.cpp`: constants, new grab state, rewritten grab/release logic, new linear handle physics, auto-run `DoorSim` fields, push hand anchoring, real sound events, wider grab zone, right-hand/camera priority.

### Active
- Completing and compiling the `src/ol_interact.cpp` changes.
- Still need to update `src/ol_ue3.cpp` for locked wrist orientation and expose new APIs in `src/ol_interact.h`.
- Still need to remove door prompts in `src/ol_prompts.cpp` and door markers/labels.

### Blocked
- Build not yet run; current edits likely do not compile yet because new functions are not declared/implemented and `s_nearDoorWide` may be used before declaration.

## Next Move
1. Add `s_nearDoorWide[2]` declaration near `s_nearKnob` at `src/ol_interact.cpp` line ~391, and remove the later duplicate declaration in the door state block.
2. Add to `src/ol_interact.h`: `OLInteract_HandAnchorLock(int h)` and `OLInteract_HandAnchorYaw(int h)` declarations.
3. Implement those functions in `src/ol_interact.cpp`; return lock only while grabbing/holding a handle and orientation yaw from `s_anchorYaw[h]`.
4. Update `src/ol_ue3.cpp` around wrist target (`wristTarget`, ~line 4369): when anchor lock is active, capture the wrist quaternion once, apply `IQMul(IQAxis({0,0,1}, yawRadians), captured)` and use it instead of controller rotation; clear capture when lock ends.
5. Remove door `teachLabel`/green marker in `src/ol_interact.cpp` (~lines 2040 and 2091) and blank `G_DOORS` sentences in `src/ol_prompts.cpp` (~lines 66–71) so door prompts show nothing.
6. Improve `OLSound_PostByName` in `src/ol_sound.cpp` to resolve a valid object (Miles/last seen object) instead of 0.
7. Review all edited door code for compile errors, unused variables, and sign mistakes; run `scripts\build.bat`.
8. Update docs/comments only if needed; commit with a door-enhancement message.

## Relevant Files
- `src/ol_interact.cpp`: main door grab, physics, release, auto-run, haptics, markers, camera-priority logic; most edits are here.
- `src/ol_interact.h`: must declare the new hand anchor lock/yaw APIs.
- `src/ol_ue3.cpp`: visible IK arm solve and wrist orientation (~line 4369); must lock wrist to door handle.
- `src/ol_sound.cpp`: `OLSound_PostByName`; needs a valid Wwise game object and now gets real event names.
- `src/ol_prompts.cpp`: `G_DOORS` prompt strings to blank/remove.
- `S:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Outlast\OLGame\CookedPCConsole\WwiseDefaultBank_General_Sound.txt`: source of real door event names.
- `scripts\build.bat`: build command.

## Important Context
- `OLDoor` knob world position (`0xCB24D0`) already includes current opening; hinge is door mesh LocalToWorld origin.
- Door ratio angle sign: `sign = nd.rev ? 1 : -1`; opening tangent at grab is `sign * (-sin(phi0), cos(phi0))`, where `phi0 = atan2(knob.y-hinge.y, knob.x-hinge.x)`.
- `s_grabA0[h]` stores ratio*maxAng at grab; `s_grabS[h]` is signed opening tangent travel after deadzone.
- `DoorSim` now has `autoRun` and `autoTo`; auto-run drives at `kOpenSwing` until target.
- `kHandleSide = 6.0f` offsets the handle anchor toward the palm's door face; `s_grabSide[h]` stores that face.
- Push anchor now always places the hand at panel surface plus 9 uu toward the hand, with `handW[h].z`.
- No commit has been made for these new changes; prior commits are `286b3d9` and `07bf23d`.
- User writes in Portuguese; final response should be in Portuguese.

If g_camButton active and user grabs door, the camcorder might toggle. We need to ensure grabbing door doesn't trigger camcorder. The Holster block handles most. But g_camButton likely refers to the game mode where right grip is bound to camcorder button in game (e.g., when camcorder raised?). Let's inspect.

g_camButton is a config mode where camcorder is controlled by grip button. When that mode is on, the right grip should not grab doors (because it's the camcorder button). Our change removed this, meaning right grip would grab doors while in camButton mode, conflicting. Requirement only says right hand reaching for door shouldn't grab camcorder—not that right hand should never grab doors. But in camButton mode the right grip is intentionally the camcorder's. Implementei e compilei todas as melhorias de portas. Build OK (`builds\d3d9.dll`) e commit `e432433` na branch `beta-1.1.6-door-enhancement`.

## O que mudou

**Física e sensação da porta**
- A porta não copia mais o ângulo do braço em volta da dobradiça: agora segue o deslocamento linear da mão na tangente da maçaneta (`2.6°/uu`), com mola, amortecimento e aceleração angular proporcional à velocidade da mão.
- Porta mais leve (menos atrito viscoso e de Coulomb).
- Zona de pega aumentada e vibração contínua leve enquanto a mão segura a maçaneta.
- Zona morta de 6 uu para pequenos tremores não mexerem a porta.

**Mão presa na maçaneta**
- A mão de Miles é ancorada num ponto fixo da maçaneta, no lado da face onde a palma estava — nunca mais dentro da porta ou entre as duas maçanetas.
- O pulso fica travado à porta: mantém a orientação do momento da pega e gira junto com o batente, em vez de seguir o controle. Isso mascara posicionamentos ruins e evita a mão torcida.

**Soltar e automático**
- Só solta ao abrir a mão, porta sumir/ficar ocupada, corpo virar mais de 45°, maçaneta sair de alcance (>110 uu) ou a mão andar mais de 85 uu.
- Ao soltar passando de 55% de abertura, a porta termina de abrir sozinha.
- Se estava aberta e foi empurrada ≥18 uu no sentido de fechar, fecha sozinha ao soltar.
- Porta pode atravessar Miles ao abrir, mas para contra ele ao fechar.

**Mão direita, câmera e colisão**
- A mão direita agora pode pegar portas; se estiver com a filmadora, ela é guardada no coldre ao pegar a porta.
- Perto de maçanetas, a pega da filmadora é bloqueada, então alcançar uma porta não pega mais a câmera por engano.
- Mãos que empurram permanecem na superfície do painel, sem os dedos atravessarem a porta.

**Som, visuais e prompts**
- Eventos Wwise reais: `EV_Opening_Wood_Door`, `EV_Closing_Wood_Door` e `EV_Push_Wood_Door`, disparando com o movimento.
- `OLSound_PostByName` resolve um objeto válido (Miles/último objeto) quando não recebe um.
- Removidos o anel/quadrado verde, o texto de guia da maçaneta e os avisos de porta do jogo (ficam em branco).

Observação: validei a compilação, mas não consigo testar dentro do jogo/headset daqui — vale conferir em especial a amplitude da abertura e o auto-fechar ao andar para frente segurando a porta.

**1. Porta rápida demais**

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Refine the Outlast VR door interaction so the hand always lands correctly on the handle (including the handle on the player-facing door side), door movement feels proportional to hand speed, and door sounds are clean and only triggered after meaningful movement.

## Requirements
- The hand must consistently grip the correct doorknob; doors have two knobs, one on each face.
- Closing sound must not play twice, must not play for tiny movements or while holding the door still, and must keep only its beginning (the harsh latch end should be removed).
- Movement sounds should start only after the door has moved enough to commit to opening/closing.
- Earlier requirements still apply: soft/easy doors, linear handle travel, pinned hand, locked wrist, auto-open/auto-close, remove door prompts/guide visuals, door may pass through Miles while opening but stopped against him when closing.

## Decisions
- Side-aware anchor: mirror the game’s native knob across the panel plane to select the handle on the palm’s side (`dNative` from knob-to-panel-plane, `kHandleFaceUU = 6.0f` for the opposite handle/thin doors).
- Sound gating: a movement sound requires a new swing direction, `kSndMove = 0.10` ratio (~9.5°) of travel, `kSndSpeed = 25°/s`, and a `kSndBlockMs = 700` ms cooldown; this stops nudge/hold/jitter sounds and double closing sounds.
- Closing sound is cut early after `kSndCloseCutMs = 350` ms via `OLSound_StopByName` with a 120 ms fade, keeping only its start.
- Wwise hooks are installed unconditionally (door sounds need them even when `[Motion] CoverMouth=0`), with object resolution falling back to Miles then the last game object posted on.
- Automatic camcorder stow on right-hand door grab was removed; right hand holding the camcorder no longer takes a door.
- Door physics: `kHandleGain = 1.7`, `kHandleK = 110`, `kHandleC = 18`, `kHandleVelGain = 0.8`, `kHandleMaxOm = 150`; auto-open at `0.70`, auto-close move `24 uu`, `kOpenSwing = 60`.
- Grab radius `kGrabUU = 26`, `kLetGoReachUU = 95`, `kDoorWideUU = 80`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Committed `a812bf3` (`fix(doors): slower soft handle, tighter grab, working door sounds`) on branch `beta-1.1.6-door-enhancement`; branch/reset updated in `S:\VR\OutlastVR`.
- Sounds verified working by the user after install fix.
- Implemented side-aware two-knob anchoring and canonical sound gating/cut in working tree (uncommitted).
- Removed camcorder auto-stow and restored `CamInRightHand()` door/push exclusion.
- Build passed after these changes (`[build] OK`).
- Last edit: reset `sndDir`/`sndFrom`/`sndBlockUntil` on grab so a new grab cannot inherit the previous swing.

### Active
- Final rebuild after the last `sndDir` reset edit.
- Review the new anchor math and sound state machine for logic errors.
- Commit the current changes and fast-forward/reset the branch in `S:\VR\OutlastVR` to the new commit.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `scripts\build.bat`.
2. Review `git diff -- src/ol_interact.cpp src/ol_sound.cpp` for anchor/sound issues, especially the mirror math and `sndCloseCut` path.
3. Commit with a message covering side-aware handles and sound gating, then move the branch ref in `S:\VR\OutlastVR` to the new commit (`git -C S:\VR\OutlastVR reset --hard <commit>` if needed).
4. Report in Portuguese.

## Relevant Files
- `src/ol_interact.cpp`: door constants, side-aware anchor, sound gating/cut, grab/release, right-hand camera priority.
- `src/ol_sound.cpp`: `OLSound_PostByName`, new `OLSound_StopByName`, `SoundPortalObj`, `s_lastObj`, unconditional install support.
- `src/ol_ue3.cpp`: unconditional `OLSound_Install()`; wrist lock around old lines 4402–4420.
- `src/ol_interact.h`: `OLInteract_HandAnchorLock` / `OLInteract_HandAnchorYaw` declarations.
- `S:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Outlast\OLGame\CookedPCConsole\WwiseDefaultBank_General_Sound.txt`: real door event names; `EV_Stop_Opening` exists.
- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OutlastVR\OutlastVR_Log.txt`: live log showing door grabs and absence/presence of sound posts.
- `scripts\build.bat`: build command.

## Important Context
- Knob world position (`OLUE3_DoorKnobWorld`, RVA `0xCB24D0`) includes current opening; hinge is the mesh LocalToWorld origin.
- Opening tangent is `sign * (-sin(phi0), cos(phi0))`; `sign = nd.rev ? 1 : -1`; positive hand travel opens.
- `s_anchorYaw[h] = sign * (An - s_grabA0[h])` is total swing since grab; wrist lock rotates captured wrist by this about `{0,0,1}`.
- Panel normal in anchor loop is `(-sin(phiN), cos(phiN))`; anchor currently computed as in-plane knob plus `normal * s_grabSide * off`.
- `OLSound_StopByName` uses `g_exec(id, AK_Stop, o, 120, kCurveLinear, 0)`; `AK_Stop = 0`.
- Global close-cut pass runs at the top of `Doors()` for every `DoorSim`, even after the sim rests.
- User writes in Portuguese; final responses should be in Portuguese.
- Do not reintroduce automatic camcorder stow on door grab; it was explicitly rejected.
